content.value: Write comments that explain intent and method contracts; distinguish comments from executable statements; keep documentation accurate.

Comments communicate information to human readers. A // comment extends to the end of a line. A /* ... */ block can span lines. A /** ... */ documentation comment can describe a class or method, including parameter meanings, returned results, and assumptions. Comments do not change the actions executed by a program.

Good documentation explains why a choice was made, what a method guarantees, and what a caller must provide. Prefer meaningful names and clear structure to comments that merely repeat a statement. A precondition describes what must already be true; a postcondition describes what the method guarantees afterward. Update the documentation when that behavior changes.

The comment explains the purpose and the division precondition. The cast in the implementation preserves fractional results. For total = 7 and count = 2, the return value is 3.5. The comment itself neither validates count nor calculates the result.

Documenting a precondition does not enforce it at run time. Comments can be wrong or outdated; trace the actual code as well. Avoid nested block-comment markers, which do not behave as independent nested comments.
Write a one-sentence contract for a method that returns the larger of two integers without changing either argument. Example: Returns the greater argument; if equal, returns their common value.
